Restarting the integration does not always seem to fix it.  It did the first 2 or 3 times I tried, but it seems to only *sometimes* fix it.
After #110928 the first refresh may not be done in time.  If you delay your automation to not trigger at startup and wait a minute or two it should work around the problem until it can be solved

Interesting.   The problems I am seeing are not shortly after startup.  My HA has not rebooted since yesterday, and this was happening this afternoon.  Is it possible that there is another situation that might lead to this problem?
I'm sure there is.. I haven't found it yet though

It looks like the is an issue with the changes introduced in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/110158

If there is no fresh data ,it no longer falls back to the group data AFIACT

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/113033 should fix the problem.

It works will my system but it needs someone else to test it

I'm willing to test it out, but I'm not sure how I'd do that...

- is this powerview gen 2 or gen 3

> 5\. This is pretty rare, and probably corresponds to situations where I rebooted the hub by power-cycling it, or restarting the integration.

> integration: Hunter Douglas PowerView (documentation, issues)

> Error fetching powerview hub 192.168.3.3 data: Powerview Hub 192.168.3.3 did not return any data: Failed to communicate with
> ```

All the rest of these should be fixed with an upstream fix - these shades dont return all data so we have to 'guess' (its not a guess, positions are mandatory based on known criteria) where the shade is

To make these assumptions the api checks which value exists and returns the ones the hub didnt. So in this case the upstream api was doing a check for ``if positions.primary:`` but this returned false when ``positions.primary == 0`` (the closed position) which is why it was so common.

review_comments: Why would we not want the current position loaded into HA at load time ?

I'm pretty sure I kept these separate for a reason, can't recall exactly but I think it was because I needed the velocity to not be affected by all return calls. The function you have changed to doesn't support velocity at all from memory 

My understanding was the velocity returned from the hub does not match that sent so we are controlling the velocity value separately in the HA database

Pulled this down to test then had the lightbulb go off...

I recall why it was seperate now - and with this in mind the ``copy_position_data`` probably needs some rework, or stick with current code

because velocity is always returned, and always returned as 0 they needed to be seperate

``update_shade_position`` would never write the hub's ``velocity`` value into HA because ``update_shade_velocity`` stored it seperately to keep the value stored in HA 

If it wasnt done this way, every call to update_shade_position would result in the velocity returning to 0 in HA too and the user could not store using the number entity
